title: No insurance?
message:
Call RotaCare: 831-333-6495
Request a free clinic appointment.
details: For uninsured Monterey Peninsula residents age 18 or older. Call 831-333-6495 to discuss your needs and arrange an appointment. The clinic lists limited in-person and telehealth sessions, plus Spanish interpreters. It does not offer dental or mental-health services. Confirm that the clinic can provide the care you need; appointments are not guaranteed.
evidence: CHOMP’s 2025 assessment, page 146, reports providing lab work and diagnostic testing to RotaCare Monterey patients. This independently documents care delivered; the clinic page supplies the current appointment route. Appointment availability and suitability for an individual were not confirmed. Supporting source: https://www.unitedwaymcca.org/sites/unitedwaymcca/files/HEalthy%20Monterey%20County/2025%20PRC%20CHNA%20Report.pdf

title: Your story isn’t over.
message:
Substance-use treatment
Call CHS: 831-237-7222.
details: CHS offers outpatient substance-use treatment and assessments. Call Salinas at 831-237-7222 or Monterey at 831-383-7800 to start with an assessment. The provider accepts Medi-Cal and lists a sliding fee for private-pay clients. Ask which program serves your age group and confirm costs and appointment availability.
evidence: Original editorial encouragement, not a quotation or a treatment-outcome claim. The CHS treatment page and 211 agree on outpatient assessments, Salinas and Monterey contact numbers, Medi-Cal and sliding fees. The provider page was reopened on November 5. Age descriptions differ, so callers should confirm the appropriate program. No appointment, insurance decision or recovery outcome was confirmed. Supporting source: https://211montereycounty.org/211-service/211montere-52247206/

title: Hidden fentanyl can stop breathing.
message:
Street drugs and fake pills can contain lethal doses.
Find naloxone. Suspected overdose? Call 911.
details: Illegally made fentanyl is a powerful opioid that may be mixed into drugs such as cocaine, methamphetamine or heroin, or pressed into fake prescription pills. A person may take it without knowing. Appearance, smell and taste cannot tell you whether fentanyl is present. An opioid overdose can slow or stop breathing and cause brain injury or death. Naloxone can reverse an opioid overdose, including one involving fentanyl. If you suspect an overdose, give naloxone if available, call 911 and stay until emergency help arrives. Naloxone does not replace emergency care. Open California Public Health’s Naloxone Finder to locate community programs; confirm hours, cost and supply with the provider. This is general prevention information, not confirmation of a specific local contaminated batch.
evidence: Rechecked November 7, 2026: CDC fentanyl guidance documents mixing into illicit drugs and counterfeit pills, potentially deadly levels and inability to identify fentanyl by sight, taste or smell. CDC naloxone guidance documents slowed/stopped breathing, brain damage or death during overdose, opioid-overdose reversal and calling 911/staying with the person. CDPH page retrieved successfully and contains Naloxone Finder; no local stock or free availability promised. Sources: https://www.cdc.gov/overdose-prevention/about/fentanyl.html ; https://www.cdc.gov/overdose-prevention/reversing-overdose/about-naloxone.html ; https://www.cdph.ca.gov/Programs/CCDPHP/sapb/Pages/Naloxone.aspx

title: One call. A different direction.
message:
Substance-use support
Call 800-952-2335 · 24/7
details: Ask Santa Cruz County’s Access team about substance-use assessment and treatment options. The 24-hour Access line is 800-952-2335. For non-emergency help Monday–Friday, 8 AM–5 PM, call 831-454-4170 at 1400 Emeline Ave., Building K, Santa Cruz, or 831-763-8200 at 1430 Freedom Blvd., Suite F, Watsonville. Ask about eligibility, coverage, referrals and available appointments. This is an access route, not a guaranteed treatment placement. For a medical emergency or suspected overdose, call 911.
evidence: The county’s urgent substance-use services page lists the Access line, office locations and weekday hours. California DHCS independently lists 800-952-2335 as Santa Cruz County’s 24/7 substance-use access number. The headline is original editorial encouragement, not a quotation or outcome claim. No provider was called and no treatment opening was confirmed. Supporting source: https://www.dhcs.ca.gov/individuals/substance-use-disorder-county-access-lines/

title: Help with your energy bill.
message:
Call 888-728-3637
Request a HEAP application.
details: Income-qualified households can request a HEAP application at 888-728-3637. Prepare a recent energy bill, household income records and the identification described in the application. If shutoff is threatened, contact your utility about payment arrangements and ask CCES for current emergency-assistance locations. Approval and available funding must be confirmed.
evidence: The City of Gonzales independently identifies CCES energy-bill assistance and the same application phone. The provider FAQ confirms required documents and the application process. Current funds and approval for any particular household were not confirmed. Supporting source: https://gonzalesca.gov/residents/gonzales-way/central-coast-energy-services-cces

title: A warmer home.
message:
Call 888-728-3637
Request a weatherization assessment.
details: CCES lists weatherization for qualifying households. Owners and renters may apply; renters need the property owner to sign the service agreement too. Call 888-728-3637 to ask about eligibility, assessment and current availability. This is an inquiry about the program, not a promised repair or installation.
evidence: The City of Gonzales and CCES describe weatherization for eligible owners and renters. The provider confirms that renters also need the owner’s agreement. No assessment appointment, installed measure or individual energy saving was confirmed. Supporting source: https://gonzalesca.gov/residents/gonzales-way/central-coast-energy-services-cces

title: Free Medicare guidance.
message:
Call HICAP: 800-434-0222
Request counseling.
details: HICAP helps with Medicare coverage, drug-plan options and billing questions. Counselors do not sell insurance. Call the HICAP program line, 800-434-0222, to request counseling. Confirm appointment options and bring your specific coverage questions. This post does not recommend a plan or promise savings.
evidence: California’s Department of Aging lists Alliance on Aging as Monterey County’s HICAP provider. The provider confirms free counseling and the program phone; its unfinished online appointment page is not used. Appointment openings and individual insurance savings were not confirmed. Supporting source: https://www.aging.ca.gov/Providers_and_Partners/Health_Insurance_Counseling_and_Advocacy_Program/Providers_List/

title: Meals at your door.
message:
Call Meals on Wheels: 831-375-4454
Request Peninsula delivery.
details: The program lists homebound seniors age 60+, veterans and adults with disabilities who have limited ability to shop or cook. Service covers the Peninsula, including Marina, Seaside and Carmel Valley. Meals have no required charge; contributions are voluntary. Use Sign Up for Meals or call 831-375-4454. Confirm eligibility, your address and a start date with staff.
evidence: County records document a 2025–26 meals contract. The current provider page describes home delivery and intake. The old contract is historical corroboration, not proof of current funding or an available delivery route. Current enrollment, route coverage and a start date must be confirmed with the program. Supporting source: https://monterey.legistar.com/View.ashx?GUID=6DEB8F28-5940-4E8F-BE87-BBB31A0FAB3B&ID=1314852&M=M

title: Meals for homebound seniors.
message:
Call Meals on Wheels: 831-758-6325
Start your Salinas Valley intake.
details: This senior program serves homebound adults age 60+ who cannot shop or cook, including temporary needs after illness or injury. Its area extends from Pajaro and Aromas to San Ardo and Bradley. Call 831-758-6325 or begin through the website Sign Up intake. Contributions are voluntary. Confirm your address, meal arrangements and start date; delivery days differ by area.
evidence: California’s Department of Aging includes Meals on Wheels Salinas in its 2025 nutrition-program stories. The provider currently publishes home-delivery eligibility and intake. Testimonials are not an independent effectiveness study. Enrollment and the first delivery date were not confirmed. Supporting source: https://www.aging.ca.gov/Providers_and_Partners/Area_Agencies_on_Aging/Older_Californians_Nutrition_Program/Success_Stories/2025/

title: 60+ and need legal help?
message:
Call 831-899-0492
Request a Legal Services for Seniors intake.
details: Monterey County residents age 60 or older can request help with housing, benefits, consumer problems, estate planning and elder abuse. The provider lists no-cost legal assistance and representation. Call 831-899-0492 or use Need Legal Help on its website to ask about intake. Case acceptance and appointment availability are determined by the provider.
evidence: Monterey County Bar Foundation identifies Legal Services for Seniors as a 2025 grant recipient providing free help to county residents age 60+. The provider confirms services and intake phone. Case acceptance, appointment availability and legal results were not confirmed. Supporting source: https://mcb-foundation.org/donors/

title: Looking for childcare?
message:
Call 831-757-0775
Get a local childcare referral.
details: For children ages 0–12, the resource page links MyChildCarePlan and the local Resource & Referral specialist at 831-757-0775. Search by location, age and schedule, or request a specialist appointment. Families must contact individual providers about open spaces or waitlists. Referral help does not mean childcare is free; ask about fees and subsidy eligibility.
evidence: California Department of Education’s indexed resource-and-referral listing matches the provider and 831-757-0775. Direct CDE retrieval was blocked; the current provider page confirms that families receive options and must contact each childcare provider about space. A referral does not secure childcare, a subsidy, or a vacant place. Supporting source: https://www.cde.ca.gov/sp/cd/re/montereyrr.asp

title: Disability equipment help.
message:
Call CCCIL: 831-757-2968
Discuss equipment and support.
sourceName: Central Coast Center for Independent Living
details: CCCIL helps people with disabilities find assistive technology, services, training and potential funding. It also describes a Voice Options device-loan pathway for people who have difficulty speaking. Contact 831-757-2968 in Salinas or 831-462-8720 in Capitola to discuss your needs. Ask about eligibility, costs and device availability before applying; equipment is not guaranteed.
evidence: 211 independently lists CCCIL assistive-technology services. A fresh provider-page fetch confirms the program and 831-757-2968. This documents assessment/device assistance, not guaranteed free equipment. Device inventory, suitability, cost and loan eligibility were not confirmed. Supporting source: https://211montereycounty.org/211-service/211montere-34285288/

title: Free job-search help.
message:
Call 831-796-3335
Book with Monterey County Works.
details: America’s Job Center staff can help with career planning, resume tools, workshops and training pathways. The provider lists these job-seeker services at no cost. Call 831-796-3335 or use the job-seeker page to get started. Ask which programs fit your situation and whether registration or an appointment is required; this is not a job offer.
evidence: The Workforce Development Board’s 2024 impact report describes job-search, training and placement support. The current service-center page supplies the contact route. The report is provider-published, not an independent job-outcome evaluation. Enrollment and any particular job or training placement were not confirmed. Supporting source: https://montereycountyworks.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/05/Monterey-County-Works-2024-Impact-Report1.pdf

title: Find food near you.
message:
Call 831-662-0991
Find your nearest Santa Cruz County food pickup.
sourceName: Second Harvest Food Bank Santa Cruz County
details: Second Harvest directs people seeking food to its Community Food Hotline and food locator. Call 831-662-0991 or follow the food-access link on its official page. Ask about a distribution near your city and confirm its hours, requirements and current supply before traveling. This is a referral route, not a promise of food at a particular site.
evidence: The City of Santa Cruz’s November 2025 statement independently recognizes Second Harvest’s food-distribution role. The current foodbank page lists its food hotline and locator. The historical funding pledge is not treated as current available funds. A hotline referral does not confirm food stock or pickup access at a specific site. Supporting source: https://www.santacruzca.gov/City-News-Press-Releases/LOCAL-AGENCIES-JOIN-FORCES-TO-SUPPORT-SECOND-HARVEST-REDUCE-FOOD-INSECURITY-DURING-SHUTDOWN

title: CalFresh paperwork?
message:
Call 831-662-0991
Request help with your application.
sourceName: Second Harvest Food Bank Santa Cruz County
details: Santa Cruz County residents can use the provider’s interest form or call 831-662-0991 to request help from its CalFresh outreach team. The interest form requests assistance; it does not approve benefits. Ask the team about current eligibility, required documents and next steps.
evidence: City recognition corroborates Second Harvest as a local food provider; its current CalFresh page documents application help and the hotline. Foodbank assistance is separate from the county’s benefit decision. Individual eligibility, benefit amount and approval were not confirmed. Supporting source: https://www.santacruzca.gov/City-News-Press-Releases/LOCAL-AGENCIES-JOIN-FORCES-TO-SUPPORT-SECOND-HARVEST-REDUCE-FOOD-INSECURITY-DURING-SHUTDOWN

title: Need diapers?
message:
Find pickup partners:
thefoodbank.org/diapers
sourceName: Second Harvest Food Bank Santa Cruz County
details: The provider lists community organizations that distribute diapers to the public and a separate list for enrolled program participants. Start with the public-distribution list, then contact the organization to check sizes, supply, hours and any requirements. Not every partner serves walk-ins, and this card does not confirm stock today.
evidence: Second Harvest is independently recognized by the city. Its diaper page identifies public distribution partners separately from partners serving enrolled clients. The card links to the public list. Diaper stock, sizes, hours and each partner’s intake conditions were not confirmed. Supporting source: https://www.santacruzca.gov/City-News-Press-Releases/LOCAL-AGENCIES-JOIN-FORCES-TO-SUPPORT-SECOND-HARVEST-REDUCE-FOOD-INSECURITY-DURING-SHUTDOWN

title: Unpaid wages?
message:
New-client instructions:
watsonvillelawcenter.org/contact
details: The center offers free legal services for low-wage people and families, including wage and workplace issues. Read the Contact page’s new-client instructions: most services require appointments and capacity is limited. Participants in its partner healthcare or CalWORKs programs can ask their provider or caseworker for a referral. Case acceptance and a response are not guaranteed.
evidence: The California State Bar’s 2026 legal-aid grant recipient list includes Watsonville Law Center. Its contact page documents public intake instructions and limited availability. Business and existing-client numbers are not presented as new-client intake. No case acceptance, legal outcome or immediate appointment was confirmed. Supporting source: https://www.calbar.ca.gov/sites/default/files/2026-01/2026%20Legal%20Aid%20Grant%20Recipients.pdf

title: A rental housing problem?
message:
Call ECHO: 831-566-0824
Request tenant-landlord counseling.
details: ECHO lists tenant/landlord information, mediation and legal-service referrals for Monterey County residents. Call its county line, 831-566-0824, to ask about the right service and current appointment options. The program page lists offices in several cities; confirm visits first. Counseling is not a promise of an attorney or rent payment.
evidence: The county’s indexed housing-program page identifies its ECHO counseling arrangement. Direct county retrieval was blocked. ECHO’s current page lists Monterey-area tenant/landlord counseling, mediation and the county phone. This is counseling/referral; no rent payment, legal representation or dispute outcome is promised. Supporting source: https://www.countyofmonterey.gov/government/departments-a-h/housing-community-development/planning-services/housing-programs

title: In critical need of pet food?
message:
SPCA · 1002 Monterey-Salinas Hwy
Saturdays · 9:30–10:30 a.m.
details: For people in critical need of help feeding their pets. The provider lists Saturday pickup, 9:30–10:30 a.m., at 1002 Monterey-Salinas Highway; follow its directions past the Adoption Center. Call 831-373-2631 to confirm before traveling. Listed limits include one bag per order and two families per car. Food types and other supplies depend on donations.
evidence: The SPCA’s 2025 report states that its Pet Food Bank distributed 152,180 pounds of food. This is a provider-reported delivery total. The current recipient page specifically says critical need and confirms Saturday pickup and limits. Current stock and food types were not confirmed. This is help during critical need, not a stock-up offer. Supporting source: https://www.spcamc.org/file_download/3c4d9cac-7c1d-4cf7-8f2a-edb5dcbeb52c

title: Support for caregivers.
message:
Call Del Mar: 800-624-8304
Request caregiver support.
details: For people caring for a family member with memory impairment or a neurological condition that began after age 18 in the three-county service area. Call 800-624-8304 or request services through CareNav. The provider lists counseling, education and support at no cost; respite may have a sliding-scale copay and depends on funding and eligibility. Confirm which services fit your situation.
evidence: A San Benito County-hosted ADRC directory independently recognizes Del Mar and its service region. That directory is historical; the current provider page supplies eligibility, contact and support options. Respite funds, copays and appointment openings must be confirmed. No caregiver health outcome is guaranteed. Supporting source: https://hhsa.cosb.us/wp-content/uploads/2023/09/Caregiver-Support.pdf

title: Need an accessible ride?
message:
Call MST: 888-678-2871
Ask how to apply for RIDES.
details: MST RIDES is shared transportation for eligible people whose disability prevents use of regular fixed-route buses. Eligibility and trip coverage require MST review; a disability alone does not establish eligibility. Service follows defined route corridors and operating hours. Call MST at 888-678-2871 or use the official information/application page and confirm fares and booking requirements before planning a trip.
evidence: MST’s published FY2025 figures report 186,167 RIDES passenger trips. Its current ADA page documents eligibility and the application process. Trips are not a count of unique people or proof of availability for a requested journey. Individual eligibility, service corridor and advance booking must be confirmed. Supporting source: https://mst.org/about-us/

title: Build your reading skills.
message:
Call the library: 831-758-7916
Join the adult tutoring waitlist.
details: The library lists individual adult tutoring for reading, writing, English-language learning and high-school-equivalency goals. Call 831-758-7916 or use the sign-up link to ask about support. The page lists a waitlist for individual tutoring, so a tutor or start date is not guaranteed. Ask about current sessions and any requirements.
evidence: The city library is a real public service, but its old adult-learning deep link returned 404 on a fresh request. Its replacement city page does not substantiate the specific tutoring waitlist and access details in this card. Held from Ready until current tutoring instructions are confirmed. Supporting source: https://www.salinas.gov/City-Hall/Departments/Library-and-Community-Services/Library

title: Find local help.
message:
Call 211 or text your ZIP to 898-211.
Free local referrals, 24/7.
details: Call 211 or text your ZIP code to 898-211 for free, confidential resource referrals, 24 hours a day. Ask about food, childcare and other local services. Tell the specialist your city and what you need. A referral does not guarantee eligibility, funding or an appointment.
evidence: United Way’s 2025 annual report documents 12,308 phone/text contacts and approximately 18,750 referrals. Its two referral totals differ slightly, so no exact referral total is repeated. Referrals are not confirmed successful assistance. No promise that a referred agency has space, funding or accepts a particular applicant. Supporting source: https://www.unitedwaymcca.org/sites/unitedwaymcca/files/Annual%20Reports/2025%20Annual%20Report%20WEB.pdf

title: Learn your bus route.
message:
Call MST: 888-678-2871
Request free travel training.
details: Everyone is eligible for fixed-route travel training. It can include planning a trip and an accompanied bus ride. Call 888-678-2871 or use the MST inquiry form to arrange training; this is not a ride booking or a promise of an immediate session.
evidence: MST is the public transit district. Its current travel-training page documents free instruction in planning and taking bus trips. System ridership does not establish a specific training-completion or independence outcome. A training appointment or personal outcome was not confirmed. Supporting source: https://mst.org/about-us/

title: Need a computer?
message:
Visit John Steinbeck Library
350 Lincoln Ave. · Ask for a guest pass.
details: John Steinbeck Library is at 350 Lincoln Avenue, Salinas. The library lists up to two hours of computer use with a library card or a guest pass from the desk. Check branch hours before visiting. A workstation may not be immediately available; printing charges are separate.
evidence: The city confirms the library system, but the old computers/Wi-Fi deep link returned 404 on a fresh request. Current guest-pass and session-length rules have not been re-established from the replacement page. Held from Ready until current computer-access instructions are confirmed. Supporting source: https://www.salinas.gov/City-Hall/Departments/Library-and-Community-Services/Library

title: Free library Wi-Fi.
message:
John Steinbeck Library · 350 Lincoln Ave.
Connect daily, 8 a.m.–8 p.m.
details: John Steinbeck Library is at 350 Lincoln Avenue, Salinas. The library lists public Wi-Fi at all locations, including adjacent parking lots, daily from 8 a.m. to 8 p.m. Building hours differ. Check the library page for connection instructions and current access.
evidence: The city confirms the library system, but the old Wi-Fi details page returned 404 on a fresh request. The replacement page does not establish the advertised 8 a.m.–8 p.m. access window. Held from Ready until the current Wi-Fi access window is confirmed. Supporting source: https://www.salinas.gov/City-Hall/Departments/Library-and-Community-Services/Library

title: Streetlight out?
message:
Send a service request:
salinasca.qscend.com/311
details: Salinas Police directs streetlight outages, graffiti, abandoned vehicles and barking-dog reports to Salinas Connect. Open Salinas Connect and choose the service-request category. This is a non-emergency service channel, not a news tip submission.
evidence: The police website identifies Salinas Connect as the city-service channel. Its linked portal returned 404 in fresh requests while the web index still showed an older portal page; the current submission route is unresolved. Held from Ready until the service-request destination loads successfully. No request was submitted. Supporting source: https://police.salinas.gov/file-a-report/

title: Check your bus.
message:
Check route changes before you go:
mst.org/service-alerts
details: Open the current service-alert page and its MST RealTime link before traveling. This card does not say that your route is running normally or that no alerts exist. Service information can change after this card is made.
evidence: MST’s official district website links its service-alerts page. This is an operational information tool for riders, not a benefit or a guarantee that every disruption has been posted. Check the live route information before traveling; no service availability or all-clear is promised. Supporting source: https://mst.org/about-us/

title: Food in Castroville.
message:
Go to 11140 Preston St.
Nov. 5 · 9–10 a.m.
details: The Food Bank lists November 5, 2026, 9–10 a.m. at Our Lady of Refuge Catholic Church, 11140 Preston Street. Check with the Food Bank before traveling. This listing does not confirm stock, required documents or eligibility; those details need provider confirmation.
evidence: The county’s indexed food-resource page recognizes this Food Bank. The current provider schedule explicitly lists 11/5/26, 9–10 a.m., Our Lady of Refuge, 11140 Preston Street. The fresh HTML and web reader agree; stale 2024 rows were excluded. Pickup operation and stock were not confirmed directly. This card expires at the listed event end. Supporting source: https://www.countyofmonterey.gov/government/departments-a-h/health/planning-evaluation-and-policy-pep/frc/food-security-resources-recursos-de-comida

title: Food in Carmel Valley.
message:
Go to 8065 Carmel Valley Rd.
Nov. 6 · 9–10 a.m.
details: The Food Bank lists November 6, 2026, 9–10 a.m. at St. Philip’s Lutheran Church, 8065 Carmel Valley Road, serving seniors and the general public. Confirm the schedule before traveling. Stock and document requirements are not confirmed.
evidence: The county’s indexed food-resource page recognizes this Food Bank. The current provider schedule explicitly lists 11/6/26, 9–10 a.m., St. Philip’s, 8065 Carmel Valley Road, for seniors and the general public. Old-year rows were excluded. Pickup operation and stock were not confirmed directly. This card expires at the listed event end. Supporting source: https://www.countyofmonterey.gov/government/departments-a-h/health/planning-evaluation-and-policy-pep/frc/food-security-resources-recursos-de-comida

title: A meal. Groceries. A place to go.
message:
150 Second St., Watsonville
Weekday lunch: noon–1 PM.
details: Visit 150 Second Street, Watsonville, for weekday lunch from noon to 1 PM. The pantry distributes supplemental groceries weekdays 9–11:30 AM and 1–3 PM. Call 831-722-4144 before traveling to confirm holiday changes and any pantry requirements. These are recipient service hours, not donation hours.
evidence: The provider publishes meal and pantry schedules. Santa Cruz Local’s December 2025 guide corroborates the location, phone and services. No same-day food stock or holiday opening was confirmed. Supporting source: https://santacruzlocal.org/where-to-find-free-food-in-santa-cruz-county/

title: Need a hot meal in Salinas?
message:
Dorothy’s Kitchen · 30 Soledad St.
Daily lunch: 1–2 PM.
details: Dorothy’s Kitchen serves breakfast 8:30–9:30 AM and lunch 1–2 PM daily at 30 Soledad Street, Salinas. Stop in during meal hours; call 831-757-3838 for changes. The separate drop-in center provides resource navigation; call 831-320-8765 for that service. Kitchen hours differ from office hours.
evidence: 211 corroborates the no-fee meal service and address. Current provider resources and contact pages specify the meal times. Meal availability on a particular day was not confirmed. Supporting source: https://211montereycounty.org/211-service/211montere-4490848/

title: Meals, showers and support.
message:
Women without stable housing:
Visit 147 El Dorado St., Monterey.
details: For women experiencing homelessness or housing insecurity. Visit the day center at 147 El Dorado Street, Monterey, Monday–Thursday 8 AM–3 PM or Friday 8 AM–noon. Ask to enroll in Next Step case management. Meals, showers and clothing have separate service times shown on the program page. Housing navigation provides applications and referrals; the center does not issue housing vouchers.
evidence: The Chamber recognizes the day center and services. The provider supplies current weekday schedules and enrollment instructions; an older Saturday listing is not reused. No shelter bed, voucher, funding award or same-day appointment was confirmed. Supporting source: https://members.montereychamber.com/list/member/gathering-for-women-monterey-4826

title: Food support for growing families.
message:
Text WIC: 888-413-2599
Ask to apply for Monterey County WIC.
details: Text 888-413-2599 to request a WIC application or breastfeeding support. The county lists eligibility for pregnancy, recent postpartum needs and children under five, subject to program and income rules. Parents, foster parents and guardians may apply for eligible children. Use the county page to check requirements and arrange your appointment; this post does not promise enrollment or a response time.
evidence: California Public Health lists Monterey County as an authorized WIC agency. The county’s own application page supplies the text-to-apply number. Individual eligibility, appointment availability and callback timing were not confirmed. Supporting source: https://www.cdph.ca.gov/Programs/CFH/DWICSN/Pages/WIC-Agencies.aspx

title: WIC helps feed young families.
message:
Call 831-722-7121
Book a Watsonville WIC appointment.
details: WIC supports eligible pregnant, postpartum or breastfeeding people and children under five with food benefits, nutrition education and breastfeeding support. Call Watsonville 831-722-7121 (18 W. Lake Avenue, Suite A) or Santa Cruz 831-426-3911 (1105 Water Street) to apply and confirm appointment hours. Eligibility depends on program and income requirements. Published Santa Cruz office days differ between pages, so confirm before traveling.
evidence: The state WIC directory lists Community Bridges and both participant phone numbers. The provider explains eligibility and appointments. Office-day inconsistencies are not presented as confirmed hours; enrollment and available appointments were not verified. Supporting source: https://www.cdph.ca.gov/Programs/CFH/DWICSN/Pages/WIC-Agencies.aspx

title: Need a ride to medical care?
message:
Call Lift Line: 831-688-9663
Apply before booking your ride.
area: Santa Cruz County · North Monterey County
details: Call 831-688-9663 to check which transportation program serves your address, age or disability, income and destination, then complete the application. Lift Line lists medical and essential trips for qualifying riders in Santa Cruz County and specified North Monterey County communities. Some programs are free; Access for All has a flat fee. Ask for the fare and reservation requirements for your trip. Office: 545 Ohlone Parkway, Watsonville.
evidence: The regional transportation commission’s 2025 guide independently lists Lift Line. The provider describes multiple programs with different eligibility and fares. No trip, vehicle availability or individual fare was confirmed. Supporting source: https://www.sccrtc.org/wp-content/uploads/2025/11/FINAL-Guide-to-Specialized-Transportation-Services-2025.pdf

title: Homebound? Meals can come to you.
message:
Call 831-464-3180 ext. 100
Request a Meals on Wheels intake.
details: For Santa Cruz County adults 60+ who are homebound and struggle to meet their nutritional needs. Call 831-464-3180 ext. 100 or complete the provider’s client application. A separate application is needed for each person. The program lists weekly frozen-meal delivery; donations are voluntary and inability to contribute does not exclude a senior. Confirm eligibility, any waitlist and a delivery start date.
evidence: Santa Cruz Public Libraries independently lists this provider and intake phone. Current delivery frequency and application instructions come from Community Bridges, rather than older directory wording. No open delivery route, waitlist position or start date was confirmed. Supporting source: https://www.santacruzpl.org/en/cid/agency/printer_friendly/421/

title: Lower the cost of staying connected.
message:
Call 866-272-0349
Find a California LifeLine provider.
details: California LifeLine discounts phone service for qualifying households. Use Provider Search at californialifeline.com, then contact a participating phone company to start the application. Call 866-272-0349 for program information, weekdays 7 AM–7 PM except state holidays. Generally one discount is allowed per household. Compare the actual plan, coverage and charges; this is not a promise of a free phone or unlimited service.
evidence: The CPUC’s current program instructions identify the enrollment route and official administrator website. Eligibility, cellular coverage, plan price and device availability must be confirmed with the participating provider. Supporting source: https://www.californialifeline.com/

title: Apply for a lower energy bill.
message:
Call PG&E: 866-743-2273
Request a CARE / FERA application.
details: CARE and FERA offer monthly bill discounts for qualifying PG&E households. Call 866-743-2273 or use the official application. Eligibility depends on household income or qualifying assistance programs and other rules. Have your PG&E account and household information ready. Request screening for the appropriate program; this does not pay an overdue balance or guarantee enrollment.
evidence: PG&E’s current residential application lists the same enrollment phone and income guidelines valid through May 31, 2027. An individual discount, approval and account eligibility were not confirmed. Supporting source: https://www.pge.com/tariffs/assets/pdf/tariffbook/ELEC_FORMS_01-9077.pdf

title: Powering medical equipment at home?
message:
Call PG&E: 800-743-5000
Request Medical Baseline enrollment.
details: Medical Baseline supports qualifying home medical equipment or heating/cooling needs with a rate-dependent allowance or discount and additional outage notifications. Apply online; your qualified medical practitioner must complete their portion. Call 800-743-5000 for application help or a paper form. Eligibility is based on medical needs rather than income. Enrollment does not guarantee uninterrupted power; retain your medical backup plan.
evidence: The current program page and provider application explainer agree on practitioner certification, non-income eligibility and the application phone. Individual medical eligibility, savings and continuous power supply are not guaranteed. Supporting source: https://www.pge.com/content/dam/pge/transcripts/medical-baseline-intro.pdf

title: Worried about your toddler’s progress?
message:
Monterey County: 831-443-1279
Request an Early Start assessment.
details: For infants and toddlers under three with suspected developmental delays or risk of developmental disability. Parents or caregivers in Monterey County can call 831-443-1279 to request an Early Start assessment through San Andreas Regional Center’s listed assessment provider. Explain the concern and ask what records are needed. This starts an assessment; it does not diagnose a child or promise eligibility for services.
evidence: California DDS and San Andreas Regional Center publish the same Monterey County Early Start assessment number. No assessment appointment, diagnosis or service eligibility was confirmed. Supporting source: https://www.dds.ca.gov/services/early-start/family-resource-center/regional-center-early-start-intake-and-family-resource-centers/

title: Veterans: get help with your claim.
message:
Call 831-647-7613
Book a benefits appointment.
details: Veterans and families can request an appointment with a county Veterans Service Specialist for benefits and claims help. Call 831-647-7613 to confirm the current representative schedule and the office that fits your location. Ask what discharge records and claim documents to bring. The county offers service in Salinas, Monterey and Marina; assistance is not a promise of a VA award.
evidence: The county publishes its service and appointment route; the statewide county veterans service officers association corroborates the phone. Appointments and individual benefits determinations were not confirmed. Supporting source: https://www.cacvso.org/county-contacts/

title: Help navigating veterans’ benefits.
message:
Call 831-454-7276
Request a county veterans appointment.
details: Call 831-454-7276 for the Santa Cruz office at 842 Front Street, or 831-763-8868 for Watsonville at 500 Westridge Drive. Ask for a benefits appointment and which records to bring. The county lists Monday–Thursday service, closed Fridays. Use the county’s current Watsonville address; an outside directory still shows an older location.
evidence: The county contact page and county veterans officers association agree on both phone numbers. The county supplies the current Watsonville address. No appointment or benefits award was confirmed; the association’s older Watsonville address is not reused. Supporting source: https://www.cacvso.org/county-contacts/

title: A hospital bill you can’t afford?
message:
Call Natividad: 831-755-4165
Apply for financial assistance.
details: Ask Financial Counseling for a charity-care or financial-assistance application for your Natividad bill. Call 831-755-4165, weekdays 8 AM–4:30 PM, or visit 1441 Constitution Boulevard, Salinas. Request the current income and documentation requirements and language assistance if needed. Eligibility depends on the hospital’s policy; this is not automatic debt forgiveness or assistance with every outside clinician’s bill.
evidence: The county hospital’s financial-assistance page and published policy agree on the application office, phone and address. An individual discount or debt cancellation was not confirmed. Supporting source: https://www.natividad.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/12/6-3100-Charity-Care-Financial-Assistance-Policy-090125.pdf

title: Find a dentist who takes Medi-Cal.
message:
Call 800-322-6384
Ask for help finding an available dentist.
details: Medi-Cal members can search by city, ZIP, language and specialty in the official dentist directory. If you cannot find a dentist accepting patients, call 800-322-6384 for assistance and interpreter access. Confirm your current dental benefits, the requested treatment and an appointment with the provider. A directory listing does not guarantee that the office has openings.
evidence: California’s official service listing corroborates the DHCS dental directory and member assistance number. Current individual coverage, treatment authorization and appointments were not confirmed. Supporting source: https://www.ca.gov/departments/217/services/1209/

title: Need health coverage or food benefits?
message:
Call 877-410-8823
Start a Monterey County application.
details: Apply for Medi-Cal, CalFresh or other county benefits by phone at 877-410-8823 or online at BenefitsCal.com. Ask which programs fit your household and what documents and interview are required. South County residents can use the King City office at 116 Broadway Street; confirm service days before traveling. The county determines eligibility; an application does not guarantee payment or coverage.
evidence: The county’s current Ways to Apply instructions explicitly name the phone application number and link the BenefitsCal portal. No individual eligibility, processing time, benefit amount or office appointment was confirmed. Supporting source: https://benefitscal.com/

title: Cash-aid help for eligible families.
message:
Call 888-421-8080
Ask to apply for CalWORKs.
details: Families can ask the county about CalWORKs cash aid and related supports. Call 888-421-8080 for application assistance, or use BenefitsCal.com. The application includes forms, an eligibility interview and verification of household circumstances. Have income and household records ready; staff will identify the required documents. This is an application route, not a guaranteed cash grant or immediate payment.
evidence: The county’s CalWORKs page explains the application and interview; its customer-service page identifies the benefit application phone. Eligibility, funding, payment timing and appointment availability were not confirmed. Supporting source: https://www.santacruzhumanservices.org/ContactUs

title: Help with benefits in the Valley.
message:
Call 831-335-6600
Book help with benefits paperwork.
details: Call 831-335-6600 to arrange enrollment or reporting assistance for CalFresh, Medi-Cal and other benefits at 6134 Highway 9, Felton. Staff also offer family advocacy and referrals. Confirm the appointment and documents to bring. This location discontinued showers, laundry, lockers and mail services in July 2025; those services are not offered in this listing.
evidence: The county housing authority lists Mountain Community Resources and the same phone. The provider specifies benefits assistance and the discontinued services. No appointment, benefit approval or grant was confirmed. Supporting source: https://hacosantacruz.org/general-information/communityresources/

title: 18–24 and without a safe place?
message:
Call 831-373-4421
Ask Safe Place about shelter access.
details: For youth ages 18–24 experiencing homelessness. Monterey Safe Place is at 590 Pearl Street, 831-373-4421, with published shelter check-in 7–9 PM; call first to confirm space and any closure. Salinas offers a navigation center at 212 N. Main Street, 831-800-2668, with drop-in services Tuesday–Sunday 10 AM–noon and 2–4 PM. Salinas is not described as an overnight shelter. Services are free in English and Spanish.
evidence: The regional homeless-services coalition’s guide corroborates Safe Place. Current ages, check-in and distinct services at each site come from CHS. No vacant bed or same-day admission was confirmed. Supporting source: https://chsp.org/wp-content/uploads/2025/02/Homeless-Services-Resource-Guide_2024-English-Version-Rev-2025.02.11.pdf

title: Help getting your child to treatment.
message:
Call 831-422-3002
Request medical-travel assistance.
area: Monterey · Santa Cruz · San Benito counties
details: For families with a child or young person from birth through age 21 diagnosed with a serious illness. Call 831-422-3002 or use the transportation inquiry form to request rides or gas assistance for medical care. Explain the appointment, destination and family’s needs. The organization serves Monterey, Santa Cruz and San Benito counties; confirm eligibility and travel arrangements before relying on a ride.
evidence: AMBAG’s regional transportation plan lists the provider and medical travel service. The provider’s current service overview and contact page supply eligibility and intake. A specific ride, gas grant or appointment transport was not confirmed. Supporting source: https://www.ambag.org/sites/default/files/2025-11/2025%20Coordinated%20Plan%20-%20Final_PDFA.pdf

title: Facing eviction? Get help early.
message:
Call 831-288-2148
Reach the Eviction Defense Collaborative.
details: Call 831-288-2148 for eviction-prevention guidance, case management and connections to partner legal or mediation services. Have your notice, lease and any court papers ready to explain the situation. The collaborative assists tenants and landlords; a call does not suspend a court deadline or guarantee an attorney, rent payment or case outcome. Ask promptly which partner can address your issue.
evidence: The county education office’s housing guide lists the eviction assistance line. Community Bridges currently describes the collaborative and access number. No representation, payment or legal outcome was confirmed. Supporting source: https://santacruzcoe.org/wp-content/uploads/2024/07/SCC-Housing-Resource-Guide-Eng.pdf

title: Parenting is hard. Get support.
message:
Call 831-465-2217
Find a free Triple P parenting class.
details: Browse current free parenting workshops in English and Spanish, then register for the session that fits your child’s age and your needs. Call 831-465-2217 for help finding a class or individual parenting support. Check each listing’s location or online format before attending. This post does not reuse an old event date or imply that every private practitioner’s service is free.
evidence: The provider currently lists November 2026 workshops and individual-support contacts. United Way’s 211 listing corroborates the program and phone. No class seat, individual appointment or family outcome was confirmed. Supporting source: https://search.211santacruzcounty.org/search/d9e2dd77-22ec-5fb4-9103-bfc4867530e6

title: Need help caring for yourself at home?
message:
Call IHSS: 831-755-4466
Start a home-care application.
details: IHSS can pay for approved non-medical home care for eligible low-income older adults and people with disabilities, including children. Call 831-755-4466 to apply. Applications can also be dropped at 730 La Guardia Street, Salinas, or 116 Broadway Street, King City. Ask about eligibility, health certification and the county needs assessment. Approval, authorized hours and provider arrangements must be determined for each applicant.
evidence: The county specifies local application contacts and locations; California Social Services confirms the county application and assessment process. No eligibility, paid hours or caregiver placement was confirmed. Supporting source: https://www.cdss.ca.gov/in-home-supportive-services/contact-us

title: You deserve to feel safe.
message:
Call 831-372-6300
YWCA domestic-abuse support · 24/7.
details: A trained domestic-violence advocate can talk through safety planning, referrals and shelter options. Call 831-372-6300 at any time; 211 lists this as a no-fee confidential service. You can ask about options without committing to leave. Contact the service from a safe device if needed. Shelter locations are confidential, and available space must be discussed with the advocate.
evidence: YWCA and 211 agree on the 24-hour domestic-abuse line and safety-planning service. YWCA reports providing safe-house nights and advocate calls in 2025; those are provider-reported activity, not an independent outcome measure. No live call answer, shelter vacancy or individual outcome was tested. Supporting source: https://211montereycounty.org/211-service/211montere-4494209/

title: Confidential help after abuse.
message:
Call 888-900-4232
Monarch’s bilingual support line · 24/7.
details: Call 888-900-4232 for confidential support regarding domestic violence, sexual assault or trafficking. Advocates offer safety planning, resources and assessment for appropriate services. The line is bilingual and operates 24 hours. Use a safe device if needed. For a planned office appointment, call Watsonville 831-722-4532 or Santa Cruz 831-425-4030; shelter arrangements are handled privately, not through a published shelter address.
evidence: Monarch’s help and contact pages and United Way’s 211 listing agree on the support line and service area. No live call response, shelter space or appointment was confirmed. Supporting source: https://search.211santacruzcounty.org/search/0019e2df-6356-5df0-8d26-a6ad2088865b

title: Get help with your water bill.
message:
Call UCAP: 831-420-5230
Ask which utility discount fits you.
area: Santa Cruz Municipal Utilities service area
details: UCAP serves qualifying SCMU households, including some tenants who do not pay the utility directly. Call 831-420-5230 for enrollment help, or choose Single-Family or Multi-Unit on the city page. Qualifying households must participate in PG&E CARE or a listed assistance program. Prepare proof of enrollment and residence; benefit cards alone may not meet documentation rules. Assistance depends on approval and available funds; it does not automatically erase overdue bills.
evidence: The city’s program and detailed enrollment pages identify the service area, assistance types, documentation and enrollment-help number. Individual eligibility, current funding and a credit amount were not confirmed. Supporting source: https://www.santacruzca.gov/Government/City-Departments/Water-Department/Santa-Cruz-Municipal-Utilities-SCMU/Financial-Assistance/Single-Family-Utility-Customer-Assistance-Program-UCAP
